To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) we propose a hierarchical infinite context model for structured prediction of linguistic structure, (ii) we use hierarchical PitmanYoris to provide a recursive smoothing form for the model, (iii) we propose A* and MCMC prediction algorithms, and (iv) we show that our model performs well in part-of-speech (POS) tagging and parsing.

we propose a novel hierarchical generative model for structured prediction of sequences and trees that is able to exploit global context and that we propose efficient algorithms for inference in this model.

we propose a new model for structured prediction which uses global context, we show how to use hierarchical PitmanYors to facilitate learning of this model and we demonstrate that the model is able to outperform Markov models on several tasks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing models for structured prediction that can capture long-range dependencies and are able to learn from limited training data.
developing models that can better capture global phenomena in structured prediction tasks.
developing models that can exploit global context in structured prediction tasks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we present a novel structured model for sequences and trees that can capture global context, and propose a hierarchical Pitman-Yor process prior for smoothing.
we present an approach to structured prediction over sequences, trees and more generally, graphs, which is able to model global context and is able to be learned in a scalable fashion.
the proposed model is able to exploit long-range dependencies in a more flexible manner than Markov models, but at a significant computational cost.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed model can be viewed as a generalization of the finite-context models, and it can be applied in a variety of tasks such as part-of-speech (POS) tagging and syntactic (dependency) parsing.
we have proposed a novel hierarchical model that exploits global context in a principled manner for sequence and tree structured prediction.
we propose an infinite context model for structured prediction, which is able to better capture long range dependencies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the global context of decisions is a rich source of structure which can help to improve performance on a variety of tasks.
global phenomena can be effectively captured using a hierarchical model that exploits an unbounded context.
global context can be incorporated into models for structured prediction in a principled way.
